headline: High: shared filesystem and shell/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; OpenMetadata’s MCP/API outputs can be consumed by xonsh without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server, while xonsh can read files and execute shell commands. That creates a plausible bridge where OpenMetadata-generated content or files can be treated as instructions by xonsh. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are written to a shared file or stream that xonsh parses as commands
IF an MCP or webhook payload from OpenMetadata is forwarded into xonsh without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic execution of any OpenMetadata-generated text in xonsh
Route OpenMetadata outputs through a strict JSON schema validator
Separate instruction channels from data channels in the orchestrator
Add a manual review step before xonsh consumes OpenMetadata artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, while xonsh can read the filesystem, environment variables, and source code and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, xonsh can expose OpenMetadata-managed data to external services or logs. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted filesystem
IF xonsh forwards files, env vars, or notebook contents to external APIs or commands
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace or container
Restrict xonsh network egress to approved endpoints
Redact secrets and environment variables before xonsh reads them
Mount OpenMetadata-managed data read-only for xonsh

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks/MCP, while xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both act on the same directory or mutable artifacts, concurrent writes and race conditions are likely, and xonsh lacks multiple-instance support. The profiles do not show locking, so the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact set
IF xonsh and OpenMetadata are run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories to each agent
Enable file locks around shared artifacts
Serialize write operations through one orchestrator
Make xonsh operate on copies instead of shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces governance and lineage outputs that xonsh can read and act on via shell commands. Because xonsh has subprocess and network capabilities, a mistaken OpenMetadata output can cascade into destructive or external actions if consumed as authoritative. No verification step is documented in either profile, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF xonsh uses OpenMetadata output as input to shell commands or scripts
IF no human or automated verification step checks OpenMetadata outputs before action
mitigations: Require validation of OpenMetadata outputs before execution
Use dry-run mode for xonsh actions
Log and diff proposed actions before applying them
Limit xonsh to read-only commands when consuming OpenMetadata data

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and lineage data, while xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables and has broad egress. If regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, xonsh may move it into external tools or logs, creating retention and residency mismatch risk. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR controls, so the safest classification is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the shared workspace or environment
IF xonsh sends that data to external APIs, logs, or notebooks
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Disable or restrict xonsh access to sensitive directories
Review retention settings for any external API calls
Add a data-classification gate before cross-agent handoff
